nodes.label: examples_test.go (parses all example programs)
nodes.rationale: Full-file feature fixtures live as .k files under examples/ and this test guarantees they all keep parsing, making examples/ a de facto regression corpus.

nodes.label: object_disambiguation_test.go (block vs object literal)

nodes.label: Release Readiness Gate
nodes.rationale: An API ships only when spec and runtime are updated, tests cover happy path plus edge cases, examples exist and no behavior ambiguity remains.

nodes.label: Deterministic Semantics and Tie-Break Rules
nodes.rationale: Semantics are specified before implementation: ordering and tie-breaking must be deterministic and null-vs-error behavior explicit, so results are reproducible and agent-predictable.

nodes.label: Deterministic Example Corpus (examples_diff.txt)
nodes.rationale: A fixed, explicitly enumerated list of examples/features/*.k programs used for branch-vs-base output comparison; the list is frozen so diffs reflect interpreter changes rather than corpus churn. Covers closures, concurrency (then_and_errors, unhandled_failures), destructuring, equality, imports, collections, match, object disambiguation, query, ranges/slices, recursion and truthy/falsy semantics.

nodes.label: Karl Unit Test Suite (tests/)
nodes.rationale: Holds lexer, parser and interpreter tests (lexer_test.go, parser_test.go, basic_expressions_test.go, object_disambiguation_test.go, parser_errors_test.go, interpreter_eval_test.go); new tests stay small and assert AST shape or evaluated value. Run with `go test ./...`, or GOCACHE=$(pwd)/.go-cache when the build cache is locked.

nodes.label: Channel<T> Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Channels communicate.

nodes.label: Sink<T> Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Sinks terminate pipelines.

nodes.label: Stream<T> Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Streams flow; kept separate from tasks/channels/sinks so the conceptual surface stays small and semantics do not blur.

nodes.label: Task<T> Abstraction
nodes.rationale: Tasks compute.

nodes.label: Race (!& / race)
nodes.rationale: A hidden race task returns the first completed child result and requests cancellation of the losers; a loser that never yields runs to completion but its result is discarded.

nodes.label: Rendezvous Channel Runtime
nodes.rationale: Unbuffered by default with a closed flag; send blocks until a receiver accepts, recv returns [value, done], and sending on a closed rendezvous is a hard runtime error.

nodes.label: Spawn and Wait (& / spawn, join task)
nodes.norm_label: spawn and wait (& / spawn, join task)
nodes.rationale: Group spawns create a hidden join task that collects child results in input order, so `& { A(), B(), C() }` yields [A, B, C] deterministically despite nondeterministic scheduling.

nodes.label: ProcessStatus
nodes.rationale: ok is true only when exit code is 0 with no signal, no timeout and no abort; non-zero exit is a status, not an implicit throw.

nodes.label: run(spec, opts?) Built-in
nodes.rationale: Blocking convenience equal to start + wait with captured stdout/stderr; output is bounded (default 1 MiB) with truncate-by-default overflow so a chatty child cannot exhaust memory.

nodes.label: Stream Backpressure (pull-driven)
nodes.rationale: Demand originates at the sink, so a slow sink slows upstream stages and the source and memory stays bounded by stage/buffer strategy.

nodes.label: Stream DAG Model
nodes.rationale: Today every pipeline expression is a linear DAG path, giving deterministic dataflow while leaving room for richer operators; tee/broadcast forking is not yet first-class, so complex topologies are composed with Task and Channel primitives.

nodes.label: Stream Execution Model (sink-triggered, lazy)
nodes.rationale: source | stage builds a lazy immutable plan; nothing runs until a terminal consumer applies, and sink execution blocks the current task unless wrapped in &/spawn.

nodes.label: partition(...) Branching Sink
nodes.rationale: Branch sources are single-consumer and unconsumed branches are dropped by policy, so an unopened branch cannot block the upstream pipeline.

nodes.label: Release v0.8.4 (spawn/race aliases)
nodes.rationale: The legacy builtin-style `spawn` runtime path was removed in favor of a single expression-based concurrency model.

nodes.label: Implementation Rules for Agents
nodes.rationale: Minimal change, preserve architecture, prefer simple over clever, avoid speculative features or redesigns.

nodes.label: Source-of-Truth Ordering (SPECS > tests > implementation)
nodes.rationale: SPECS/ is design input, tests/ is the behavioral contract, implementation is last; semantic changes must update specs in the same change set so the three never drift.

nodes.label: Stream Model Guardrails
nodes.rationale: No push-based execution and no implicit buffering, because either would break backpressure guarantees that bound memory use.

nodes.label: Phase-1 Debugger Concurrency Policy
nodes.rationale: Only the main evaluation task is controlled; breakpoints in child tasks are not guaranteed. This keeps the first cut small and predictable and avoids global stop-the-world complexity, deferring task-aware debugging to phase 2.

nodes.label: Language Influences (JavaScript, Scala, Go)
nodes.rationale: JavaScript for prototyping speed and JSON-like data, Scala for expression-oriented pattern matching, Go for concurrency as a language primitive (adapted to an event-loop model).

nodes.label: Process Parser Constraints (& proc rejected)
nodes.rationale: `& proc(...)` and `spawn proc(...)` are parse-rejected because proc already starts immediately and returns a waitable handle; wrapping it in a task would be redundant and misleading.

nodes.label: Karl Error Handling Model
nodes.rationale: Recoverable/runtime errors get explicit recovery via `? { ... }`; stream/process execution paths stay structurally fail-fast so partial pipelines do not silently continue.

nodes.label: Cooperative Cancellation
nodes.rationale: Cancellation takes effect only at yield points (wait/send/recv/sleep/http); awaiting a canceled task raises a recoverable error with kind = "canceled".

nodes.label: Recoverable Errors (`?`) Runtime Semantics
nodes.rationale: `?` now applies to any expression and catches both RecoverableError and RuntimeError, binding `error` as { kind, message }. exit(), parse errors and control-flow misuse stay uncatchable so hard stops remain hard.

nodes.label: Task Failure Policy (fail-fast / defer)
nodes.rationale: Errors are stored on the task handle and surface on wait; unobserved detached failures fail the run fast by default, with defer reporting them at program end.

nodes.label: Yield Points
nodes.rationale: Only wait, ch.send, ch.recv and sleep yield; everything else is synchronous, so a task that never yields monopolizes the loop.

nodes.label: Recover Operator `? { ... }`
nodes.rationale: There is no Result/Ok/Error type; explicit failure via exit() and narrow recoverable failures via `?` keep the error model free of type ceremony.

nodes.label: Playground Parse Error UX
nodes.rationale: Parse errors gained file:line:column spans plus a source excerpt and caret, replacing bare messages that gave no location.

nodes.label: Stream Error Model and Recoverable Kinds
nodes.norm_label: stream error model and recoverable kinds
nodes.rationale: Structural fail-fast: a failing source/stage/sink terminates the current pipeline execution rather than skipping items.

nodes.label: Stream Member Reads (s.read()/s.close())
nodes.rationale: read() is stateful per stream value instance with one lazily-opened cursor and no implicit restart after EOF; concurrent read() on the same instance is a recoverable stream_state error.

nodes.label: Next Language/Runtime Improvements
nodes.rationale: Wanted: select-like primitive, defer/finally cleanup, time/duration ergonomics, safer optional access, scheduler/trigger runtime, newline-as-statement-boundary parsing, string interpolation.

nodes.label: Runbook Production-Hardening Blockers
nodes.rationale: Structured errors, durable checkpoints, a secrets/config boundary with redaction, and an observability API are what remain between a runnable port and production use.

nodes.label: Release v0.3.4 (task-failure policies)
nodes.rationale: fail-fast became the default for unobserved detached task failures so silent partial failures do not pass unnoticed; defer remains for end-of-run reporting.

nodes.label: Deadlock Probe Correctness Rule
nodes.rationale: Runtime deadlock probing must not misclassify external-event waits (e.g. top-level signalWatch(...).recv()) as deadlocks.

nodes.label: Collection Error Semantics
nodes.rationale: Invalid argument types and invalid key-domain transitions are runtime errors; missing keys return null/false rather than panicking, and no host-language panic may escape.

nodes.label: Block vs Object Disambiguation Rules
nodes.rationale: `{` starts a block by default; it is an object literal only when empty, containing a top-level `:`, a spread, or a trailing comma. Shorthand-only objects need the trailing comma precisely to break this ambiguity. Newlines are whitespace and never terminate statements.

nodes.label: Object vs Map Distinction
nodes.rationale: Objects are fixed identifier-keyed shapes; Maps carry dynamic keys. Object keys must be identifiers so shapes stay statically readable.

nodes.label: Recoverable Errors: Broad vs Narrow
nodes.rationale: Making every runtime error recoverable is judged inadvisable: it blurs expected failure and programmer bugs, lets typos (unknown members) be silently recovered, and risks continuing after partial side effects. Feasible but requires grammar, evaluator and spec changes.

nodes.label: Safe Accessors / get-or Helpers Proposal
nodes.rationale: Middle ground: keep `?` for call expressions and add explicit safe accessors (obj.get, arr.get, obj.has) or a dedicated safe member/index operator rather than making all runtime errors recoverable.

nodes.label: Trailing Array as Program Return Value
nodes.norm_label: trailing array as program return value

nodes.label: Recoverable Block (? operator with implicit error)
nodes.norm_label: recoverable block (? operator with implicit error)

nodes.label: Screenshot Showcases Karl Feature Surface in a Real Editor
nodes.norm_label: screenshot showcases karl feature surface in a real editor

nodes.label: Evaluator Execution Hooks (beforeNode/afterNode)
nodes.rationale: Hooks carry source location, node kind and frame depth; with no debugger attached the cost is a near-zero branch and return.

nodes.label: Karl Debugger (CLI First)
nodes.rationale: Built terminal-first so one engine can later be exposed to DAP clients; time-travel and reverse execution are explicit non-goals for phase 1.

nodes.label: Event Loop Runtime Architecture
nodes.rationale: Target model is a single-threaded cooperative scheduler with no preemption and CSP-style rendezvous messaging; the current Go implementation uses goroutines instead.

nodes.label: loom (runtime)
nodes.rationale: Chosen for its strong execution/scheduling metaphor, a natural fit for Karl's concurrency narrative.

nodes.label: plain (formatter)
nodes.rationale: One clear style to minimize formatting bikeshedding.

nodes.label: Collection Naming Rules
nodes.rationale: Ordered-tree search vocabulary (floor/ceil/predecessor/successor/closest) stays distinct from hierarchy vocabulary (parent/children/siblings/ancestors/descendants); aliases require explicit approval.

nodes.label: Interpreter Known Limitations
nodes.rationale: Direct AST evaluator with no bytecode/JIT, goroutine-backed tasks with nondeterministic scheduling, eager range allocation, and no tail-call optimization.

nodes.label: Karl Tooling Naming System
nodes.rationale: Concrete metaphors over abstract jargon, short CLI-friendly names, consistent tone. It is a product vocabulary spec, not a mandatory implementation plan.

nodes.label: Release Workflow (tag v*)
nodes.rationale: CGO_ENABLED=0 with -trimpath -ldflags '-s -w' produces small, reproducible, statically linked cross-platform binaries; Windows packages via PowerShell Compress-Archive because tar/zip differ on that runner.

nodes.label: GitHub Pages Static Deploy Workflow
nodes.rationale: The workflow probes the Pages API first and no-ops with a notice when Pages is disabled, so forks and unconfigured repos do not fail CI.

nodes.label: bench (Karl Playground)
nodes.rationale: Browser-first playground so Karl can be tried with zero install; also runnable locally via `karl playground`.

nodes.label: Pipeline Operator `|` in Grammar
nodes.rationale: `|` is placed between logic_or and logic_and in precedence and is type-checked at runtime rather than statically, because Karl has no type system.

nodes.label: Karl Playground (browser)
nodes.rationale: Running the interpreter client-side in WASM removes the need for any backend execution service.

nodes.label: Playground WASM Runtime (runKarl bridge)
nodes.rationale: cmd/wasm exposes runKarl(source) to global JS scope; JS overrides window.fs.writeSync to capture Go-runtime stdout/stderr into the output pane.

nodes.label: Stream Pipeline Operator `|`
nodes.rationale: `|` is reserved exclusively for stream pipelines; left operands must be sources/plans/readers/<process>, right operands stages or sinks, validated at runtime.

nodes.label: Karl Product Context (between Bash and Go)
nodes.norm_label: karl product context (between bash and go)
nodes.rationale: Karl deliberately targets the gap between Bash and Go: CLI tools, pipelines, infrastructure scripting, process orchestration and DevOps automation.

nodes.label: Playground Browser Limitations
nodes.rationale: No filesystem access, restricted sockets, and main-thread execution that can block the UI for large programs.

nodes.label: Stream WASM Runtime Limitation
nodes.rationale: In the browser runtime low-level stream/file APIs may be unavailable and return recoverable stream errors instead of hard-failing.

nodes.label: Notebook Runner
nodes.rationale: notebook.go Runner executes cells against a single persistent environment and emits CellOutput records; exposed programmatically via LoadNotebook/NewRunner/ExecuteNotebook.

nodes.label: .knb Notebook JSON Format
nodes.rationale: Notebooks are plain JSON (title, description, version, cells, metadata) so they are diffable, hand-editable and require no editor/server.

nodes.label: Notebook --output Results JSON
nodes.rationale: Persists notebook definition plus per-cell outputs (cell_index, type, value, timestamp) so runs are machine-checkable rather than terminal-only.

nodes.label: Notebook State Persistence Across Cells
nodes.rationale: Enables incremental, narrative workflows (load -> transform -> analyze) where later cells build on bindings from earlier ones.

nodes.label: Loop-as-Expression (for ... with ... then)
nodes.rationale: Loops carry accumulator bindings via `with` and yield a value via `then`, with `break v` supplying an early result — so iteration composes as an expression instead of mutating outer state.

nodes.label: REPL Persistent Environment
nodes.rationale: Bindings survive across evaluations for the whole session, which is what lets multi-step examples be typed line by line.

nodes.label: 02-functions-closures.knb (Intermediate)
nodes.rationale: Teaches first-class functions, the makeAdder closure pattern, composition and reduce/accumulation.

nodes.label: 04-advanced.knb (Advanced)
nodes.rationale: Showcases Karl's distinctive features: match guards, for-loops as expressions, destructuring and the recover (?) operator.

nodes.label: makeAdder Closure Example
nodes.rationale: Canonical demonstration of lexical capture (`makeAdder = n -> x -> n + x`) reused across REPL, notebook and docs.

nodes.label: compose / First-Class Function Example
nodes.rationale: `compose = (f, g) -> x -> f(g(x))` demonstrates curried, function-returning-function syntax as the idiomatic Karl shape.

nodes.label: Match Expression with Guards Example
nodes.rationale: `case _ if n < 0 -> ...` shows guard clauses layered on wildcard patterns with a final catch-all arm.

nodes.label: karl.tmLanguage.json TextMate Grammar
nodes.rationale: Grammar scopes (e.g. keyword.operator.async.karl, keyword.operator.arrow.karl) are theme-agnostic so the extension works with any VS Code color theme and users can override colors via editor.tokenColorCustomizations.

nodes.label: Karl (Bench Light) Color Scheme
nodes.rationale: Optional scheme reusing the bench/landing token palette (#1e1e1e, #bd93f9, #ff79c6) so the editor matches the playground/landing brand.

nodes.label: vsce package -> karl-lang-0.1.0.vsix
nodes.rationale: VSIX is the shareable artifact installable via `code --install-extension` or `cursor --install-extension`, and the precursor to Marketplace publishing.

nodes.label: Async Operator Highlighting (& spawn, !& race)
nodes.rationale: Karl's concurrency is expressed in single-character operators that would otherwise blend into the code, so & and !& are given prominent, deliberately distinct scopes to make concurrent flow visually obvious.

nodes.label: Karl Built-in Function Catalog (highlighted)
nodes.rationale: Enumerates the stdlib surface the grammar recognizes: runtime/IO (log, http, httpServe, fromJson, toJson), SQL (sqlOpen/sqlExec/sqlQuery/sqlBegin/sqlCommit/sqlRollback), concurrency (rendezvous, send, recv, done, then, wait, sleep, signalWatch), UUID/time/hash (uuidNew, now, timeParseRFC3339, sha256), collections (map, set, filter, reduce, sum, find, sort, length), strings and fail.

nodes.label: karl trace dap Debug Adapter Bridge
nodes.norm_label: karl trace dap debug adapter bridge
nodes.rationale: Reuses the Debug Adapter Protocol so VS Code/Cursor can debug .k files with F5 (Karl: Debug current file); resolves the interpreter from PATH or the KARL_BIN override.

nodes.label: VS Code Marketplace Publishing Flow
nodes.rationale: Publisher account + Personal Access Token, vsce login, vsce publish; afterwards installable as ext install karl-lang.karl-lang.

nodes.label: Karl Sublime Text Syntax
nodes.rationale: Installed by copying Karl.sublime-syntax and Karl.sublime-color-scheme into Packages/Karl; by default it inherits the user's existing theme rather than forcing a look.

nodes.label: karl-lang 0.1.0 Initial Release
nodes.rationale: 2026-01-29 first release: full keyword/operator/built-in highlighting, async operator scopes, comments, auto-closing pairs, bracket matching and smart indentation.

nodes.label: Three Extension Installation Methods
nodes.rationale: Copy into ~/.vscode/extensions (fastest for local use), vsce package into a .vsix (for distribution), or F5 Extension Development Host (for iterating on the grammar).

nodes.label: Karl Language Support (VS Code Extension)
nodes.rationale: MIT-licensed extension (karl-lang 0.1.0) registering the .k file association, syntax highlighting, bracket/auto-close behavior and a debug bridge for VS Code and Cursor.

nodes.label: VS Code Extension File Structure
nodes.rationale: package.json manifest, language-configuration.json for brackets/auto-close, syntaxes/karl.tmLanguage.json for the grammar, plus docs, LICENSE, .vscodeignore and test.k as the highlighting fixture.

nodes.label: Karl Editor Plugins
nodes.rationale: Umbrella directory covering the VS Code/Cursor extension and the Sublime Text syntax; `make vscode-reinstall` is the sanctioned install path from repo root.

nodes.label: Reload Window Activation Requirement
nodes.rationale: A freshly copied extension folder is not picked up until the window reloads, which is the single most common cause of 'no highlighting' reports; the troubleshooting path is reload, verify .k extension, then check the language mode.

nodes.label: Hierarchical Node Tree ntree(...)
nodes.rationale: A separate type exists because ordered trees rebalance internally, so their parent/child links are implementation artifacts; exposing them would be unstable and misleading. ntree keeps parent/children as user-level semantics with stable node identity.

nodes.label: Ordered Index Tree tree(kind?)
nodes.rationale: AVL/treap ordered index giving O(log n) lookup and bounds; keys must be homogeneous ordered scalars because mixed key domains have no total order.

nodes.label: For-Expression Evaluation Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Loop-state updates are explicit in the body; `continue` must preserve progress or the loop may not terminate. `break` with no value runs `then`; `break expr` bypasses it.

nodes.label: Member Call Desugaring (no implicit receiver)
nodes.rationale: Dot-calls on built-in collections are pure syntax sugar (list.map(fn) -> map(list, fn)); user-defined objects get no implicit receiver so functions must take the object explicitly.

nodes.label: Truthy/Falsy Semantics
nodes.rationale: Python-style: null/false/0/0.0/""/[]/{}/empty map/set/tree are falsy; logical operators return Bool rather than the operand.

nodes.label: Collection Design Goals
nodes.rationale: Collections must be useful for real programs, explicit about asymptotic behavior, predictable across CLI/REPL/bench, and composable with Karl expression style.

nodes.label: Debugger Expression Evaluation in Frame
nodes.rationale: print/watch evaluate normally in the selected frame; side effects are the user's responsibility in phase 1, with a safe-eval subset deferred.

nodes.label: Debugger Frame Tracking
nodes.rationale: Explicit call frames are required to implement stack, frame, locals and frame-scoped print.

nodes.label: Notebook Runner
nodes.rationale: A stateful executor holding one persistent Environment so later cells can reference bindings from earlier cells.

nodes.label: Notebook Minimal Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Standard-library-only dependencies, JSON format, direct evaluation with no extra layers - chosen so the system stays easy to understand, quick to run, and simple to extend incrementally.

nodes.label: Karl as a Practical Systems Language
nodes.norm_label: karl as a practical systems language

nodes.label: Karl Playground
nodes.rationale: Zero-setup browser environment served by `karl playground` on localhost:8081/bench so newcomers can run Karl without installing a toolchain.

nodes.label: syscall/js Go-to-Browser Bridge
nodes.rationale: Bridges the Go WASM runtime to JavaScript; interpreter stdout is captured by a custom JS polyfill and rendered in the output pane.

nodes.label: REPL Colon Commands (:help :quit :examples :env :clear)
nodes.rationale: A leading colon namespaces meta-commands so they can never collide with valid Karl expressions.

nodes.label: Karl REPL (karl loom)
nodes.rationale: Interactive read-eval-print loop invoked as `karl loom`; auto-prints the last expression's value so exploration needs no explicit print calls.

nodes.label: Automatic Multi-line Input Detection
nodes.rationale: The REPL detects an incomplete expression and switches to a continuation prompt instead of requiring an explicit line-continuation marker.

nodes.label: Karl Remote REPL (loom serve / loom connect)
nodes.norm_label: karl remote repl (loom serve / loom connect)
nodes.rationale: Plain-TCP line protocol (default localhost:9000) so the session is reachable not only from `karl loom connect` but from nc, telnet or rlwrap — network transparency without a custom client requirement.

nodes.label: WASM Rebuild Step (GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm)
nodes.rationale: Because the playground ships a prebuilt binary, core language changes are invisible until karl.wasm is rebuilt from ./wasm and the server restarted.

nodes.label: Client-Side WASM Interpreter
nodes.rationale: Compiling the interpreter to assets/playground/karl.wasm keeps execution entirely on the user's machine: no backend server to run, and no user code is ever sent over the network (security + zero hosting cost).

nodes.label: Remote REPL Has No Authentication
nodes.rationale: The server intentionally ships without auth; the documented mitigation is to bind only on trusted networks or tunnel via SSH (ssh -L 9000:localhost:9000) rather than exposing 0.0.0.0 publicly.

nodes.label: Equality Semantics (== identity, eqv structural)
nodes.rationale: == is identity for composites and eqv is deep for arrays/objects/maps; mixed-type comparison is always false because there is no implicit coercion.

nodes.label: Pattern Matching Semantics
nodes.rationale: Tuples are represented as arrays and there is no tuple literal, so tuple patterns are just fixed-length array patterns. Call patterns are unsupported.

nodes.label: Expression-Based Language Design
nodes.rationale: Everything evaluates to a value so complex operations flow into a single binding ('return to the left').

nodes.label: match Expression
nodes.rationale: One pattern-matching construct handles all branching, keeping the conceptual surface small.

nodes.label: Karl Design Philosophy
nodes.rationale: Small conceptual surface, composable primitives, predictable runtime behavior, explicit error handling, strong streaming guarantees.

nodes.label: `->` Single Meaning Principle
nodes.rationale: `->` always means binder-to-expression, in lambdas and in case arms alike, so the syntax has no context-dependent readings.

nodes.label: Explicit Complexity Contracts
nodes.rationale: Every API states O(1)/O(log n)/O(n) targets in docs and specs, and any API claiming optimization must carry benchmark coverage proving it.

nodes.label: Karl API-First Stdlib Skill
nodes.rationale: Skill for designing/reviewing Karl stdlib APIs for collections, streams, processes and runtime primitives, applied when user-land algorithms should be promoted into optimized built-ins.

nodes.label: Hierarchical Node-Tree API (parent, children, siblings, ancestors, descendants)
nodes.norm_label: hierarchical node-tree api (parent, children, siblings, ancestors, descendants)
nodes.rationale: Semantic hierarchy gets a dedicated API because AVL/Treap internal structure must never be exposed as stable parent/child semantics — balancing can rearrange it.

nodes.label: Ordered Tree Search API (closest, floor, ceil, predecessor, successor, range)
nodes.norm_label: ordered tree search api (closest, floor, ceil, predecessor, successor, range)
nodes.rationale: Ordered trees must expose the searches users actually need at O(log n) instead of forcing them to call keys() and hand-write binary search.

nodes.label: API Proposal Output Contract
nodes.rationale: Every proposal must ship signatures, return shapes, complexity targets, determinism/tie rules, error/null behavior, one realistic example and a minimal test matrix.

nodes.label: OpenAI Agent Manifest for API-First Stdlib Skill
nodes.norm_label: openai agent manifest for api-first stdlib skill
nodes.rationale: Interface block (display_name, short_description, default_prompt) exposing the skill to an OpenAI-style agent runtime: design APIs at the highest useful abstraction level while preserving determinism and performance contracts.

nodes.label: API Review Checklist
nodes.rationale: Six gates before merging a stdlib API: problem fit, surface quality, semantic precision, performance contract, AI ergonomics, release readiness.

nodes.label: AI-Friendly API Ergonomics
nodes.rationale: Names stay short, explicit and discoverable and return shapes small and stable, with aliases avoided — the target consumer is an AI agent that should solve tasks by composing built-ins only.

nodes.label: Prefer API-Level Solutions Over User-Land Algorithms
nodes.norm_label: prefer api-level solutions over user-land algorithms
nodes.rationale: Users should compose high-level primitives, not re-implement textbook algorithms in app code; a repeated known algorithm is a signal to promote it into a built-in, while speculative abstractions without concrete use cases are rejected.

nodes.label: Square Outline Frame Containing the Monogram

nodes.label: System Primitives (argv/env/environ/programPath/readLine)
nodes.rationale: The runtime context snapshot is captured at evaluator startup and shared by spawned tasks and imported modules, so argv/environ stay stable across a run.

nodes.label: proc(spec, opts?) Built-in
nodes.rationale: Starts execution immediately and returns a waitable/abortable handle, so there is no separate start step to forget.

nodes.label: Process Spec Object
nodes.rationale: Unknown fields are rejected rather than ignored, so typos in spec/opts fail loudly.

nodes.label: Stream/Process Integration Points
nodes.rationale: <process> is accepted directly as a stream source shorthand for its piped stdout, so `p | lines() | collect()` works without reaching into p.stdout.

nodes.label: Example Corpus Diff Against Base Branch
nodes.norm_label: example corpus diff against base branch
nodes.rationale: Fixed example corpus outputs are diffed against the PR base branch so semantic regressions in the interpreter surface as output drift, not just test failures.

nodes.label: Karl Jupyter Kernel
nodes.rationale: Provides a Jupyter frontend for Karl so notebook users get code execution, state persistence and error reporting without leaving the Jupyter ecosystem; installed as a kernelspec pointing at the karl binary.

nodes.label: Kernel Cross-Cell State Persistence
nodes.rationale: Variables and functions defined in one cell must remain available in subsequent cells for an interactive workflow to be useful.

nodes.label: Karl Notebook System
nodes.rationale: A deliberately minimal Jupyter-like notebook runner (`karl notebook`) built on static JSON files, trading interactive editing and rich output for a small, dependency-free implementation.

nodes.label: Notebook --step and --repl Interactive Modes
nodes.rationale: --step gates each cell on confirmation for teaching/debugging; --repl runs everything then drops into an interactive session to append new cells, bridging static notebooks and the live REPL.

nodes.label: kernel/install.sh Kernelspec Installer
nodes.rationale: Builds the karl binary and writes kernel.json into ~/Library/Jupyter/kernels/karl so Jupyter discovers Karl automatically instead of requiring manual spec authoring.

nodes.label: ZeroMQ Kernel Transport (go-zeromq/zmq4)
nodes.rationale: Jupyter's wire protocol is ZeroMQ-based, so the kernel uses github.com/go-zeromq/zmq4 for socket management and message handling in kernel/kernel.go rather than inventing a transport.

nodes.label: Per-Client Isolated Sessions
nodes.rationale: Multiple clients may connect simultaneously but each gets its own environment, so concurrent users cannot clobber one another's bindings.
